section_summary: This section records late December 1934 and early January 1935 efforts by American and British officials and oil companies to negotiate changes to Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law. It includes an embassy despatch with a conversation memorandum and a summary of Japanese press articles, followed by telegrams and correspondence about proposed talks with Japanese officials.

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Turner
people.role: Standard-Vacuum Oil Company representative; surname uncertain in OCR

subfiles.title: Telegram on December 27 oil representations
subfiles.about: Reports American and British representations to Kurusu and his tentative support for talks with oil company representatives.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu received the representations sympathetically and proposed talks, pending consultation with the Vice Minister for Commerce and Industry.

subfiles.title: Letter to Kersey F. Coe on oil representations
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Relays the Embassy’s report of the December 27 representations and possible talks with Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Coe that Japanese officials were receptive but had not yet committed to a conference.

subfiles.title: American Oil Interests in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports proposals for a joint company protest and introduces two enclosures on Japan’s petroleum policy.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes Japanese companies’ difficulties with the law, Matsukata’s interest in higher gasoline prices, and Tokyo Asahi articles arguing that Japan could withstand a foreign oil supply cutoff.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Kojiro Matsukata
subfiles.about: Records Matsukata’s proposals for compromise between foreign oil companies and the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Matsukata urged foreign firms to join a petition for higher gasoline prices and suggested a staged oil storage compromise. Dickover explained the firms’ concerns about investment, uncertain returns and the six-month storage requirement.

subfiles.title: Summary of Tokyo Asahi articles on petroleum protests
subfiles.about: Summarizes November 1934 articles defending Japan’s petroleum controls and assessing foreign oil supplies.
subfiles.summary: The articles defend Japan’s sales quotas and storage rules, dispute objections to the Manchukuo oil monopoly, and argue that alternative suppliers could offset a foreign company boycott. They also discuss domestic and Manchurian fuel substitutes and suggest that Manchukuo’s monopoly might precede one in Japan.

subfiles.title: Telegram on press report of American representations
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese press coverage of the American oil representations.
subfiles.summary: A Washington news despatch reported the American representations; Grew had seen no similar report about the British ones.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on sharing telegram 286
subfiles.about: Considers whether to relay hopeful news from Tokyo to Standard-Vacuum’s New York office.
subfiles.summary: The writer favors letting the company’s agents in Japan convey the news and asks for concurrence.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese readiness for oil company talks
subfiles.about: Reports Kurusu’s response to proposed talks and possible adjustments to petroleum rules.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu said commerce officials welcomed talks, foreign refineries could share in demand growth, foreign importers would receive some increased demand, and storage provisions needed adjustment. Company representatives were expected to begin talks around January 7.

subfiles.title: Letter to Kersey F. Coe on proposed conference
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that Japanese commerce officials welcomed discussions with oil company representatives.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck relays the Foreign Office representative’s view that talks would be worthwhile.

subfiles.title: Telegram seeking guidance on joint oil company talks
subfiles.about: Asks whether American and British oil representatives should seek joint talks with Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: Standard-Vacuum representatives had arrived from Shanghai. Grew saw value in a united company approach but sought the Department’s guidance before advising them.

subfiles.title: Department telegram advising joint oil company talks
subfiles.about: Advises Grew that American and British oil representatives should seek joint conferences.
subfiles.summary: The Department favors joint talks while emphasizing that the companies themselves must decide.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum acknowledgment to Hornbeck
subfiles.from: Kersey F. Coe, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Department letters and reports representatives’ travel from Shanghai for talks in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Coe says a misunderstanding has been cleared up and promises to share news from the forthcoming discussions.
